verses.text: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.
When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
By justice a king brings stability to the land, but a man who exacts tribute demolishes it.
A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.
The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.
Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.
Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.
A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.
If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.
The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
A king who judges the poor with fairness— his throne will be established forever.
A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law.
A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.
An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.
A man's pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.
A partner to a thief hates his own soul; he receives the oath, but does not testify.
The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
Many seek the ruler's favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.
An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.

context.author: Solomon; these proverbs “were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah” (25:1), about 250 years after Solomon
context.genre: Wisdom sayings: comparisons, word pictures and contrasts
context.audience: The people of Judah, and especially those who served the king (25:2-7)
context.setting: Hezekiah’s collection closes with warnings and promises. “A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery” (v.1). “When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan” (v.2). The righteous care about justice for the poor (v.7). “A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back” (v.11). “Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law” (v.18). Pride brings a man low, but a humble spirit obtains honor (v.23). “The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high” (v.25), and justice comes from the LORD, not from the ruler’s favor (v.26).
context.custom: “Vision” (v.18) is the word used for a prophet’s revelation from God (1 Samuel 3:1; Isaiah 1:1). Without God’s word, people run wild, as Israel did when they made the golden calf (Exodus 32:25, the same verb for “cast off restraint”). A servant who is pampered from youth will grieve his master in the end (v.21); household servants were part of many families.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 30 brings the words of Agur, a humble man who asks God for neither poverty nor riches.
context.timelineBible: “In those days the word of the LORD was rare and visions were scarce” (1 Samuel 3:1). Amos warns of a famine “of hearing the words of the LORD” (Amos 8:11). Jesus says the humble will be exalted (Matthew 23:12), as in v.23.

translation.meaning: A prophetic vision, a revelation from God, not a plan for the future. Without God’s word the people run wild.
To let loose, to run wild. Used of Israel at the golden calf (Exodus 32:25).
A bird trap. Fear of people catches a man like a bird.

gospelParallels.note: Whoever humbles himself will be exalted (v.23).
Am I trying to please people? Then I would not be Christ’s servant (v.25).

otBackground.note: Visions were rare in those days.
The people were running wild at the golden calf.
A famine of hearing the words of the LORD.

overview.summary: Hezekiah’s collection ends: accept correction, rule justly, control your anger, hold to God’s word, and trust the LORD rather than fearing people.

history.t: Isaiah and Micah spoke in Hezekiah’s time.
The king’s justice made a land stable.

customs.t: Traps of string and wood caught birds.
Servants lived as part of the family.

archaeology.t: A clay seal impression found on the Ophel and announced in 2018 may name Isaiah the prophet; the reading is debated.
Egyptian tomb paintings show nets and snares for catching birds.

overview.discussion: “The fear of man is a snare” (v.25). Whose opinion of me am I most afraid of, and what would trusting the LORD change?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (25:1)

timeline.label: Pride and the fear of man
